housing: St Helens is a former glass-making and coal-mining town between Liverpool and Manchester. Much of the housing is Victorian and Edwardian red-brick terraces in Thatto Heath, Parr and Sutton, with large post-war council estates and inter-war semis in Eccleston, Rainhill and Rainford. Private renting grew faster than the regional average between 2011 and 2021, much of it in the terraced streets. Prices remain well below the North West average.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces in Thatto Heath, Parr and Sutton: record the back yard, rear alley gate, gutters, chimneys and any damp in rear rooms.
Homes on former mining land: photograph any cracks in walls or ceilings and doors or windows that stick, which may come from ground movement.
Former council houses in Parr and Haydock: photograph the boiler, fencing, sheds and gardens, and note any non-standard construction.
Stone cottages in Billinge: check walls inside for damp, and photograph window reveals and chimney breasts.
New-build homes on former industrial sites in Sutton and Newton-le-Willows: photograph snagging items, sealant, paintwork and the garden.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems can contact St Helens Borough Council's Private Sector Housing Standards Team, which can inspect homes and take action against landlords.
